notes: Most complete fix, including the quoted "{}" branch adjustment that the reference also makes, with extensive parser, dispenser and adapter-level tests; however, it repeats inline quoted checks everywhere instead of a helper and mixes wasQuoted==0 with Quoted() inconsistently.

Semantically matches the reference at every site, including the anonymous-block and `{}` branches, but uses repetitive inline checks that mix `Quoted()` and `wasQuoted == 0` instead of a helper; tests are thorough, including snippet and adapter-level cases.

Clean token helper methods applied at every structural brace check, matching the reference, but it leaves the pre-existing quoted "{}" branch untouched, so a quoted "{}" starting a new line still doesn't split segments; good dispenser and parser tests.
Same structure as the reference using Token helper methods, with complete coverage apart from the minor `{}` branch; tests cover nested blocks and backtick-quoted braces.

Essentially the reference approach with Token methods covering all brace checks (only the quoted "{}" newline edge is left as-is), and thorough tests including nested blocks, own-line quoted braces and an unterminated-block error case.

Near-identical to the reference with idiomatic Token methods, covering dispenser, parser and anonymous-block sites; it only leaves the pre-existing quoted-`{}` new-line branch unchanged, and its tests are solid.

Fixes the core issue but misses the doImport anonymous-block key check, and it changes unrelated behavior: a quoted {block}/{blocks.*} is no longer substituted, which could regress existing snippet configs; parse tests only check segment counts.

Clean Token helper methods that fix the issue, but it leaves the anonymous-block `"{"` check unchanged, leaves the `{}` branch as before, and adds an unrequested behavior change that stops quoted `{block}`/`{blocks.*}` from expanding in snippets.

A claimed-module map gives the same semantics as C2: it fixes the root-module for_each case but keeps resource-level parent/child dedup, so child imports of different instances are still silently discarded. Tests are thorough: a unit test with fixture plus plan and apply regressions.

Fixes the reported same-module for_each case, but still dedups by ConfigResource across modules, so a parent import silently drops every child import for that resource, even ones targeting different instances; the unit, plan and apply tests are good but only cover the non-conflicting cases.

Keeps every import block and resolves parent/child overrides by statically parsing each target instance and checking it against all collected statements. This fixes the reported case and static cross-module overlaps. Dynamic (for_each) targets are treated as always overlapping, so a child's non-conflicting instances get dropped. Module-instance keys are not compared at expansion, unlike the reference's dedup at expansion time; the single added test covers only the basic case.

Cleanest approach of the four: it checks each new statement against all earlier ones by static instance address, so non-overlapping parent and child imports both survive. It still over-drops when a target is dynamic and lets a child win for keyed module instances, whereas the reference defers dedup to expansion; it adds only one plan test.

Simple ancestor check fixes multiple blocks for one resource within the same module. It still drops every child-module import for a resource whenever the parent imports any instance of it, so non-overlapping child instances are lost silently, the same class of bug.

Same semantics as C1 via a `moduleIsAncestor` scan: it fixes the same-module case but any ancestor import for a resource silently discards all descendant imports for other instances of it; it adds a single root-module plan test.

Instance-level static dedup is similar to C1, but the claimed map stores only the most recently appended statement per resource. A child import can therefore slip past a parent override when the parent has several blocks, or when the child's own earlier block updated the claim. That makes the result order-dependent and fragile, though it adds two decent plan tests including a module case.

Statically compares instance addresses to keep non-overlapping parent and child imports, but `claimed` holds only the last statement per resource, so with several parent blocks a child block can slip through and overwrite the parent's import ID; keyed module instances and dynamic `to` expressions are also only approximated.
